title: Domain models
description: Generated from the domain_models package. Do not edit: change the models and run `make -C domain_models schemas`.

harness.description: The ACP agent, for example ``opencode`` or ``claude-code``.
harness.title: Harness

model.description: The model it runs, for example ``anthropic/claude-opus-5-5``.
model.title: Model

Approval.description: PROVISIONAL: who approves what is open (review item 8).

digest.description: What the approval covers: for a planned workstream, the story digest approved.
digest.title: Digest

Approval.title: Approval

CapabilityManifest.description: Everything a workstream VM may do. What it is granted equals this, and nothing more.
CapabilityManifest.title: CapabilityManifest

Component.description: The parts of the system that act on their own.
Component.title: Component

Convo.description:
A conversation outside the system that bears on one or more workstreams.

A pull request, a chat thread, an email chain, or the comments on a tracker issue. Used to route
follow-up events to the workstreams attached to it, and to send replies back where they were asked.

external_id.description: Its stable ID in that system.
external_id.title: External Id

pull_request.description: Set exactly for a pull request.

Convo.title: Convo

ConvoEvent.description:
One event in a convo: a message, a review comment or verdict, a CI result, a state or label change.

Used to start and inform the sessions of the workstreams attached to the convo. Append-only. Its body
is untrusted.

at.description: When it happened in its system.
at.title: At

external_id.description: Its ID in the convo's system, so a second delivery is recognized.
external_id.title: External Id

ConvoEvent.title: ConvoEvent

ConvoEventKind.description: PROVISIONAL: grows with the feedback loops (review item 10).
ConvoEventKind.title: ConvoEventKind

ConvoLink.description:
Attaches one convo to one workstream, and says why.

The convo started the workstream, the workstream created it, or it was attached later. Follow-up
events in the convo go to every workstream attached to it.
ConvoLink.title: ConvoLink

Epic.description:
The workstreams that come from one plan DAG: the breakdown of one OpenSpec change.

Used to follow the progress of a plan as a whole. An epic is never executed itself: it is done when
all its workstreams are.

change.description: The OpenSpec change whose breakdown the epic's stories come from.
change.title: Change

ticket_id.description: Its ticket, when epics are mirrored to a tracker.
ticket_id.title: Ticket Id

Epic.title: Epic

ExternalActor.description: Someone in another system the system cannot attribute to a person it knows.
ExternalActor.title: ExternalActor

ExternalIdentity.description: One account a person holds in another system, so events from that system can be attributed to them.

subject.description: The account's stable identifier in that system, not its display name.
subject.title: Subject

handle.description: The name people see, for example a GitHub login. Informational; it may change.
handle.title: Handle

ExternalIdentity.title: ExternalIdentity

digest.description: The content digest the VM started from. A name alone is never enough.
digest.title: Digest

Membership.description:
One person's role in one project.

Used to decide what that person may see and do in the project. A person has at most one membership
per project.
Membership.title: Membership

NetworkRule.description: One internet host a VM may reach.

host.description: A host name. Never an IP address or a range.
host.title: Host

NetworkRule.title: NetworkRule

Person.description:
A human who uses the system: plans, approves, steers, or asks for work.

Used to attribute every action, to grant roles in projects through memberships, and to recognise the
same person in other systems through their external identities.
Person.title: Person

Project.description:
A body of work: its repositories, its spec store, and its members.

Everything else belongs to a project. It scopes who may see and do what, and which repositories
sessions may change.

repositories.description: Every repository of the project. Exactly one has the ``spec_store`` role.
repositories.title: Repositories

Project.title: Project

ProjectRole.description: What a member may do in one project. Each role includes the ones before it.
ProjectRole.title: ProjectRole

ResourceMount.description: A named resource the worker provides, mounted read-only. The project never names a host path.

resource.description: For example ``go-module-cache``. Each worker maps the name to its own storage.
resource.title: Resource

path.description: Where it appears inside the VM.
path.title: Path

ResourceMount.title: ResourceMount

Schedule.description:
A recurring request: each time it fires, it creates a scheduled workstream with its goal.

Used for cron-like work, such as dependency updates or nightly checks. PROVISIONAL: cron ownership
is open (review item 13).

cron.description: A five-field cron expression, evaluated in UTC.
cron.title: Cron

Schedule.title: Schedule

Session.description:
One agent conversation with one purpose, run in its workstream's VM.

For example, drafting a change, reviewing it, or addressing review comments. The unit a worker runs
and acp-broker relays; a retry is a new session. Records who held it, how it ended, and what it cost.

attempt.description: 1 for the first session of this stage in the workstream; a retry adds one.
attempt.title: Attempt

statement.description: The agent's own account of why it stopped, after secret masking.
statement.title: Statement

Session.title: Session

Source.description: Where a workstream came from, and where its replies go.

requester.description: Who asked. None only for a scheduled workstream.
requester.title: Requester

schedule_id.description: The schedule that created it, for a scheduled workstream.
schedule_id.title: Schedule Id

reply_to.description: The convo replies go to. None when the requester reads replies in the workbench.
reply_to.title: Reply To

origin_url.description: A link to the message, issue, or comment that started it.
origin_url.title: Origin Url

Source.title: Source

StoryRef.description: The plan node a planned workstream implements. The story itself lives in the spec store.

change.description: The OpenSpec change the story belongs to.
change.title: Change

digest.description: The story digest (planlib) of the version this workstream implements.
digest.title: Digest

StoryRef.title: StoryRef

Ticket.description:
The tracker record of a workstream or an epic, kept in the system's own database.

People find and discuss work through it, and it is mirrored to external trackers (Huly, Jira,
Linear) in either direction. A ticket has no state of its own: its state is its subject's, and each
mirror maps that state to its tracker's states.
Ticket.title: Ticket

TrackerMirror.description: A ticket's copy in one external tracker. PROVISIONAL: sync and conflict rules are open (review item 3b).

instance.description: Which installation, for example ``https://huly.example`` and its workspace.
instance.title: Instance

external_id.description: The tracker's stable ID for the issue.
external_id.title: External Id

external_key.description: The key people see, for example ``ONS-77``.
external_key.title: External Key

synced_at.description: When the last sync in either direction finished.
synced_at.title: Synced At

TrackerMirror.title: TrackerMirror

Worker.description:
A trusted machine that runs workstream VMs.

Used to place each VM on a worker that offers every capability and resource the VM needs, and to
know which workers are online.
Worker.title: Worker

WorkerOffer.description: What a worker allows the VMs it runs.

capacity.description: The worker's total, after its own reserve.

resources.description: The named resources it can mount.
resources.title: Resources

WorkerOffer.title: WorkerOffer

Workstream.description:
One unit of work, from the moment it is asked for until it is done or cancelled.

A planned story, an ad-hoc ask, or a scheduled run. The central record: sessions run for it, its
ticket shows it in trackers, its convos carry the discussion about it, and its events record
everything that happened to it.

epic_id.description: The epic of a planned workstream. None for the others.
epic_id.title: Epic Id

story.description: Set exactly for a planned workstream.

goal.description: What done means, in words. For a planned workstream, from its story.
goal.title: Goal

repositories.description: The project repositories its sessions change.
repositories.title: Repositories

blocked_by.description: Workstreams that must be done before this one starts.
blocked_by.title: Blocked By

owner.description: Who answers for it. None only for a scheduled workstream without an owner.
owner.title: Owner

participants.description: Everyone who acted on it, the owner and requester included.
participants.title: Participants

vm_id.description: Its VM, from the first session until the VM is removed.
vm_id.title: Vm Id

Workstream.title: Workstream

WorkstreamEvent.description:
One entry in a workstream's history.

A state change, an approval, a session starting or ending, a steer, an escalation, or a decision.
Used to show people what happened and why, and to give later sessions that context. Append-only:
never changed or deleted.

summary.description: One line a person can read.
summary.title: Summary

WorkstreamEvent.title: WorkstreamEvent

WorkstreamEventKind.description: PROVISIONAL: grows with the lifecycle (review item 4).
WorkstreamEventKind.title: WorkstreamEventKind

WorkstreamState.description: PROVISIONAL: the lifecycle is open (review item 4).
WorkstreamState.title: WorkstreamState

WorkstreamVm.description:
The one VM a workstream's sessions run in, from its first session until the workstream closes.

Records which worker runs it, the image it started from, and the capabilities it asked for and was
granted. Untrusted: everything the agent runs is inside it.

declared.description: What the project's manifest asks for.

granted.description: What the worker actually applied, as it reported. It must equal ``declared``.

WorkstreamVm.title: WorkstreamVm
